blocks.title: What paint protection film is, and what it stops.
body: Paint protection film is a **clear film** laid over the painted panels of your vehicle. When a rock comes off the truck ahead of you, the film takes the hit and the paint under it stays as it was.

It is a different job from a ceramic coating. A coating is a thin chemical layer for gloss and easy washing, and **it is not armor**: it will not stop a rock chip. Film is the physical layer. Plenty of people want both, film where the chips happen and a coating for the shine.
checks: **Takes the chips.** Rock chips and road debris hit the film, not your paint.
**Clear.** The film goes on clear, so your paint color is what people see.
**Your coverage.** Tell us which panels you want covered and we quote exactly that.

blocks.title: The panels most people cover first.
blocks.intro: Rocks hit the front of a vehicle and the lower edges. These are the places people usually start. Tell us what you want covered and we quote exactly that.

items.title: Front bumper
items.body: The lowest, most forward panel on the vehicle, and the one that meets most of the rocks on highway trips.

items.title: Hood and fenders
items.body: The leading edge of the hood and the front of the fenders collect chips fast, and they are the panels you see from the driver's seat.

items.title: Mirrors
items.body: Mirror caps stick out into the air and pick up chips and scuffs.

items.title: Rocker panels and lower doors
items.body: Your own tires throw sand, salt and gravel at the lower sides, which is why they chip and pit over a few Michigan winters.

items.title: Door edges and handle cups
items.body: Small panels that take keys, rings and fingernails every day. Ask about them when you ask about the front end.

blocks.title: Five steps from free quote to film on the paint.
blocks.intro: Film covers what is under it, good or bad, so the paint gets cleaned up before any film goes on.

steps.title: Start with a free quote
steps.body: Tell us what you drive and which panels you want covered. Photos of the paint help us tell you whether it needs any polishing first.

steps.title: Drop-off or valet pickup
steps.body: Film is installed at our Clinton Township shop, by appointment. Bring the vehicle to us, or ask about our [pick-up and drop-off valet service](/mobile-detailing/): we pick it up and bring it back.

steps.title: Wash and decontamination
steps.body: A full decontamination wash: iron and tar removal, then a clay treatment, so nothing is trapped between the film and the paint.

steps.title: Polish if the paint needs it
steps.body: Swirls under the film stay under the film. If your paint has them, [paint correction](/paint-correction/) can come first, quoted with the film so you see one number.

steps.title: Film goes on, indoors
steps.body: The film is fitted panel by panel in our enclosed bays, out of the dust and weather that would otherwise end up under it.

faq.q: How much does paint protection film cost?
faq.a:
It depends on the vehicle and how much of it you want covered, so we quote it per vehicle instead of publishing a price list. A front bumper and mirrors is a very different job from the whole front end.

Tell us what you drive and which panels you want covered, by text, by phone or with the quote form on this page, and we will give you a real number. Financing is available through Affirm and Klarna.

faq.q: Should I get paint protection film or a ceramic coating?
faq.a:
Start with what worries you. If it is rock chips on the front end, that is what paint protection film is for: a coating will not stop a chip. If it is gloss, water spots and easier washing, that is what a [ceramic coating](/ceramic-coating/) is for.

Many people do both, film on the panels that take the hits and a coating for the shine. Ask us and we will tell you honestly which one fits what you are worried about.

faq.q: Will paint protection film fix the chips and swirls I already have?
faq.a:
No. Film is clear, so what is under it stays visible under it. A chip is a spot where the paint is gone, and film will not put it back.

Swirls and light scratches can be polished out before the film goes on. If your paint needs it, we quote [paint correction](/paint-correction/) together with the film.

faq.q: Can you install paint protection film at my home?
faq.a:
No. Film goes on at our Clinton Township shop, in enclosed bays, because dust and weather are the enemy of a clean install.

If getting to the shop is the obstacle, use our pick-up and drop-off valet: we pick the vehicle up, do the work at the shop and bring it back.

faq.q: How long does a paint protection film install take?
faq.a:
It depends on how many panels you cover and whether the paint needs polishing first. A few front panels is a much shorter job than a full front end with correction.

We give you an exact window when we quote your vehicle, so you can plan around it or book the valet.
